permission.description: Allow raising the shell's main management window. Granted to both remote webviews (the harness workbench at http://127.0.0.1:<port> and the DeepSeek official chat at https://chat.deepseek.com) so the injected pull-string launcher can bring the panel to the foreground on either surface; tauri-build only exposes app commands to capabilities through an app-level permission file like src-tauri/permissions/app-commands.json, so an explicit allow-list is required for any remote webview to invoke the command.
Allow the loopback harness webview to report a one-shot white-page health failure to the management panel.

Allow the loopback harness webview to ask how many milliseconds its self-heal reload should back off while a cross-shell package operation is in flight. Measured on 2026-09-30: a reload that landed mid-uninstall died again within seconds; the reload itself was right, its timing was not. The command only reads the package-activity beacon.

Allow the loopback harness webview to hand the shell the text the user has typed but not yet sent, so it survives a reload or a window rebuild. The script calls it ~600ms after typing stops, not on unload (an IPC started while the page is going away rarely lands).

Allow the loopback harness webview to take that draft back once it has been written into the composer. Read-and-delete on purpose: a draft left on disk would reappear out of nowhere the next time the user opens the workbench normally.

Allow the loopback harness webview to drop the stashed draft once the composer is empty again. Sending a message clears the Lexical editor programmatically, which fires no input event, so the page reports the emptiness itself; without this command the already-sent message would sit on disk and be typed back into the composer the next time the workbench opens. Separate from stash_harness_draft on purpose: the reason to delete lives in the page's state ('we stashed something and now there is nothing'), not in the text.

Allow every app command from the shell's own local windows (the management panel). Defining ANY app-level permission flips Tauri from 'app commands are open to local windows' to 'app commands require an explicit grant', so this permission restores the pre-existing behavior for the local UI. Maintenance: every command added to `tauri::generate_handler!` in lib.rs must be listed here, or its invoke from the panel fails with 'not allowed. Command not found'. This invariant is enforced by scripts/check-invariants.mjs in CI.

Read-only cloud subscription usage for the standalone subscription window (label "subscription-viewer", opened by the overview card's「套餐用量」button via open_subscription_window). The window renders the cached/fetched MiniMax token-plan tiers and DeepSeek balances via get_subscription_usage, jumps to the local model-usage window via open_usage_window, and opens the workbench via open_harness so the user can edit the model credentials it reuses — no write, settings or lifecycle commands.

Read-only usage stats for the standalone model-usage window (label "usage-viewer", opened by the overview card's「模型用量」button via open_usage_window). The window renders the aggregated 90-day view via get_model_usage and closes itself — no write or lifecycle commands.

Tab-control commands plus the pull-string lamp's focus raise for the official-chat window's local strip webview (label "official-chat-strip", the index.html?chatstrip=1 SPA route). The strip renders the tab bar and calls the tab commands to read the fixed tab list and switch the active content webview; the lamp (pullstring-launcher.js, injected straight into the strip because a separate launcher webview can't be made transparent on this Tauri 2.11 / wry 0.55.1 stack) calls focus_main_shell to raise the management panel over the cursor. Granted only to the local strip webview — the remote content webviews (chat.deepseek.com / www.qianwen.com / agent.minimaxi.com) never get them because chat-fingerprint.js deletes window.__TAURI__ there, and the capability has no remote matcher.

Read-only log access for the standalone log viewer window (label "log-viewer", opened by open_log_window). The window lists files via list_log_files (categorized sidebar) and renders one file's tail via read_log_file; nothing else. The panel keeps the full command set via allow-local-commands.
